notes.headline: Nomura’s McElligott says AI is now too big to fail as a $41 billion leveraged ETF bid builds
notes.judging_note: 본인 발언 확인. 조건부 표현 있음: 발동 가격 기준이지 지금 나오는 물량 아님.

excerpts.text: McElligott says Jensen Huang’s return has triggered $41 billion in leveraged ETF buying tied to AI stocks.
McElligott cautions that much of this demand comes from automated trading rather than fresh investor conviction.
The Nomura strategist sees massive mechanical buying behind AI stocks, but warns the flows run on autopilot rather than conviction Nomura’s Charlie McElligott set the market a deadline last Thursday.
McElligott’s original setup was a clean experiment.
According to the research findings on McElligott’s view, AI stocks may see leveraged ETF flows reach up to $41 billion in a single session.
McElligott is applying the “too big to fail” framing to AI.

notes.headline: Nomura's Charlie McElligott: Jensen Is Back — The AI Rescue Trade Unleashes a $41 Billion Buying Frenzy.
